flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Bot Management
flags.description:
<s1-nav>From the soledrop.co button at the top of the page, swap over to the one-flare.com Security Rules page. Click on the Mitigate Definite Bot Traffic rule.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Cloudflare allows users to customize their security rules. For this specific rule, what is the response code sent after blocking?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="400">The flag is the response code</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Security Insight
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Go back to Security rules. Find the Traffic Sequence button next to Documentation.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Traffic Sequence shows the simplified journey of a request as it proxies through a Cloudflare configuration. 

Looking at the flow, what feature is used right before a request reaches the origin server? </s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="Rate limiting">The flag is the name of the box preceding Origin server</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 3 - Security Insight
flags.description:
<s1-nav>While in the Traffic Sequence window, click on Workers. Select the shop-soledrop-worker from any row. Select Metrics from the nav bar at the top. Set the event window to the last 30 days.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Cloudflare Workers is a serverless platform for building, deploying, and scaling apps across Cloudflare's global network without needing complex configuration. The shop.soledrop.co site from before was deployed using a custom worker. Under Request Distribution we can see the locations where a Worker ran to handle an incoming request.

Find the city where this worker was deployed the most.</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="Dallas">The flag is the name of the city</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF HA Equivalent
flags.description:
<s1-nav>From the menu on the left navigate to Build. From the dropdown select AI then open Workers AI.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Like standard Cloudflare Workers. Workers AI allow users to deploy LLMs and AI agents across Cloudflare's global network.

From the model catalog, what is the name of the model that can perform Automatic Speech Recognition?</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="anthropic/...">The flag is the name of the model</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 5 - AI Prompt Injection
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-AI-PromptInjection — LLM Prompt-Injection Probing of SoleDrop Concierge /api/v1/chat in the Alert name column.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="30">The flag is the number of alerts in this cluster.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 6 - Attempt
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-AI-PromptInjection — LLM Prompt-Injection Probing of SoleDrop Concierge /api/v1/chat in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
When a single source IP issues five or more chat POST requests within five minutes, what kind of attempt is this indicative of?</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="brute-forcing">The flag is the name of the attempt.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is in the Purple AI Overview.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Enrichment
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigation instructions here...</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Oftentimes, analysts will append contextual data fields—such as agent specs, file hashes, and user details—to reduce manual triage time. These are referred to as Enrichment fields.

Take a look at the enrichment field that would display the number of injection posts.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="{{Function.DEFAULT...}}">The flag is the value associated with injection_posts</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is <s1-answer>{{Function.DEFAULT(Function.JQ(create-power-query.body.data.data, "(.[0] // [])[1] | values | floor", true), "N/A")}}</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 8 - Default URL
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to HyperAutomation. Open the workflow designated 'See WAF Rule'. Add the Cloudflare integration named 'Get zero trust user failed logins'.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
What is the default URL before any account or user information has been input?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="https://api.cloudflare...">The flag is the default URL.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 9 - Error Message JSON Body
flags.token: CTF{Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/account_id/access/users/user_id/failed_logins, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?}
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to HyperAutomation. Open the workflow designated 'See WAF Rule'. Add the Cloudflare integration named 'Get zero trust user failed logins'.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Paste that URL into a web browser. What is the error message in the json body?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="Could not ...">The flag is the error message.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is <s1-answer>Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/account_id/access/users/user_id/failed_logins, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 10 - Failed Login Attempt
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to HyperAutomation. Open the workflow designated 'See WAF Rule'. Add the Cloudflare integration named 'Get zero trust user failed logins'.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Test the given Workflow and see the correct response when the account and user information has been input.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the time the failed login occurred.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is the value of the datetime field.
